content:
Apple is turning 50 this year, and many of its customers are even older than the company itself. The company has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, mainly through accessibility settings.

The methods cover a wide range, from adjusting the font size on Apple Watch to setting your iPhone to notify you when the washing machine finishes a cycle...

Apple says its goal is to make technology accessible to everyone, including older users.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone, including older users. That's why our products and services are designed with inclusivity in mind, featuring built-in accessibility functions that help you connect, create, and engage with what you love in the way that suits you best. As life changes, the way we interact with the world changes too. From enlarging on-screen text to making conversations clearer in noisy restaurants, Apple's range of devices, features, and services are designed to flexibly meet your needs.

The support page mainly lists accessibility features, divided into ten categories.

  • Vision: View screen content more comfortably
  • Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Adjust how you navigate and control your devices
  • Speech: Speak in your own way
  • Cognitive: Stay focused and in control
  • Personalisation: Create a personalised experience
  • Organisation: Remember what matters
  • Health: Stay on top of your health with practical insights
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay connected

Taking the Vision category as an example, it includes options such as enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colours, setting colour filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing on-screen motion. Some features, like Sound Recognition, though heavily promoted by Apple at launch, remain little known to this day.

Sound Recognition detects specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to send a notification when they're detected. The feature can identify 15 different sounds, and users can also train their devices to listen for their own name, as well as unique electronic sounds in their environment, such as beeps from kitchen appliances, certain types of alarms, or doorbells. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect smoke or carbon monoxide alarm sounds. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay, where your iPhone will listen for and identify sounds such as sirens, horns, and even a baby crying. When a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — and if you're using CarPlay, the notification will appear directly on your car's display.

This page comprehensively organises the various accessibility features available on Apple devices, and is packed with content. Each item lists instructions separately for the different supported devices, which — depending on the feature — may include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.
